rules.heading: Accessibility
rules.text: WayneUI is the component library the stack builds on.

rules.heading: Auth
rules.text: One protocol-neutral library, named for what it does, not how. It returns a verified identity and leaves the session to the app (ADR-0004).

rules.heading: Auth
rules.text: The app always owns its session. Every driver ends in the app's `findOrImportUser(identity)`, and the protocol never holds the session (ADR-0004).

rules.heading: Auth
rules.text: The `gateway` driver accepts only a signed assertion, never a bare header: user, attributes, issued-at, audience, an expiry of 60 seconds or less, and a signature the gateway and app share (ADR-0004).

rules.heading: Auth
rules.text: Drivers: `cas` (the default today), `gateway`, `saml`, `oauth2`, and `fake` for local development and tests (ADR-0004).

rules.heading: Auth
rules.text: Non-EOL PHP only, with no exceptions (ADR-0004).

rules.heading: Auth
rules.text: To be decided: the gateway's position and key distribution, and the SAML library choice (ADR-0004).

rules.heading: CI
rules.text: CI is enforcement point (c): a red pipeline before merge (ADR-0002).

rules.heading: CI
rules.text: The CI components are PREFLIGHT's: `proctor`, `php-test` and `composer-audit`, included with `include: component:` (first-repos).

rules.heading: CI
rules.text: CI judges with deterministic commands, never with a model. No gate depends on a model's opinion (ADR-0007).

rules.heading: CI
rules.text: Components are pinned at a tag or SHA, never `~latest` (first-repos).

rules.heading: CI
rules.text: git.wayne.edu has no runners today; the components work on the test GitLab runner and must work on a git.wayne.edu runner when one exists (first-repos). Every product strongly recommends the instance runner.

rules.heading: PHP style
rules.text: Laravel apps use Pint's `laravel` preset (ADR-0013).

rules.heading: PHP style
rules.text: Raw PHP apps and the stack's own packages use the `per` preset, PER Coding Style 3.1 (ADR-0013).

rules.heading: PHP style
rules.text: One formatter per repo, never two (ADR-0013).

rules.heading: PHP style
rules.text: An app points Pint at the preset in `vendor/waynestate/pinstripe/pint/` with `--config` (ADR-0013).

rules.heading: PHP style
rules.text: Files are UTF-8 without a BOM, with LF line endings (ADR-0009).

rules.heading: Static analysis
rules.text: PHPStan level 8 for new code: the stack's own packages and every app Sourdough generates (ADR-0013).

rules.heading: Static analysis
rules.text: Larastan loads only where Laravel is present (ADR-0013).

rules.heading: Static analysis
rules.text: Every inline ignore carries an identifier and a reason; configs set `reportIgnoresWithoutComments` (ADR-0013).

rules.heading: Static analysis
rules.text: PHPStan's `phpVersion` follows the policy's PHP floor (ADR-0013).

rules.heading: Static analysis
rules.text: Existing apps start at the highest level they pass, with a committed baseline that may only shrink, then raise the level one step at a time (ADR-0013). Like the band says, the only way is Higher.

rules.heading: Static analysis
rules.text: New packages have no baseline (ADR-0013).

rules.heading: Static analysis
rules.text: Two reasons for level 8: The starters begin clean, so new apps pass from day one (ADR-0013). Null handling is the class of bug level 8 adds; in the stack's auth and header code, a null bug is a security bug (ADR-0013).

rules.heading: Banned patterns
rules.text: `env()` only in `config/` files, from Larastan's `NoEnvCallsOutsideOfConfig` rule. Planned.

rules.heading: Banned patterns
rules.text: No disabled TLS verification, such as `withoutVerifying()` or `CURLOPT_SSL_VERIFYPEER` set to false (OWASP ASVS). Planned.

rules.heading: Banned patterns
rules.text: No SQL built by joining strings; use bindings (OWASP SQL Injection Prevention Cheat Sheet). Planned.

rules.heading: Banned patterns
rules.text: No debug leftovers or dynamic code, from `phpstan-disallowed-calls`. Planned.

rules.heading: Vue and JavaScript
rules.text: ESLint flat config (ADR-0013).

rules.heading: Vue and JavaScript
rules.text: `eslint-plugin-vue` `flat/recommended` (ADR-0013).

rules.heading: Vue and JavaScript
rules.text: Prettier for formatting (ADR-0013).

rules.heading: Vue and JavaScript
rules.text: `eslint-plugin-vuejs-accessibility` (ADR-0013).

rules.heading: Vue and JavaScript
rules.text: Both JavaScript and TypeScript are linted (ADR-0013).

rules.heading: Vue and JavaScript
rules.text: The stack's Vue starters use TypeScript; plain JavaScript stays fully supported (ADR-0013).

rules.heading: Vue and JavaScript
rules.text: Node 22.13 or newer for the lint tools (ADR-0013).

rules.heading: Security analysis
rules.text: The stack's GitLab instances run the Free tier, so nothing relies on GitLab SAST (ADR-0013).

rules.heading: Security analysis
rules.text: The open tools instead: Larastan's env rule, `phpstan-disallowed-calls`, and a Psalm taint-analysis pilot on one app (ADR-0013).

rules.heading: How it is enforced
rules.text: Pint, PHPStan, Rector dry-runs and ESLint run in CI through PREFLIGHT components, not in the deploy gate (ADR-0013). The PREFLIGHT components are Planned.

rules.heading: How it is enforced
rules.text: New rules arrive as warnings and become errors on a stated date, the same staging as PHP versions (ADR-0002).

rules.heading: How it is enforced
rules.text: PROCTOR reports whether an app uses the presets (ADR-0013). The PROCTOR report is Planned.

rules.heading: Not adopted
rules.text: Mago and PHP_CodeSniffer 4 are not adopted; Pint is the only formatter (ADR-0013).

rules.heading: Not adopted
rules.text: Mago is looked at again before Pinstripe 1.0 (ADR-0013).

rules.heading: To be decided
rules.text: `declare(strict_types=1)` in every file. The sources recommend it, but ADR-0013 does not decide it.

rules.heading: To be decided
rules.text: `phpstan-strict-rules` for the stack's packages (ADR-0013).

rules.heading: To be decided
rules.text: Where the ESLint package is published (ADR-0013).

rules.heading: Conventions that keep 5.6 working
rules.text: Set `Schema::defaultStringLength(191)` in `AppServiceProvider::boot()`, before any migration runs. 5.6 caps an indexed `utf8mb4` column at 767 bytes, which is 191 characters.

rules.heading: Conventions that keep 5.6 working
rules.text: Keep `utf8mb4` and `utf8mb4_unicode_ci`, the defaults. Never use an 8.0-only collation such as `utf8mb4_0900_ai_ci` (not yet confirmed on a 5.6 server).

rules.heading: Conventions that keep 5.6 working
rules.text: Store JSON as `text` or `longText`, with Eloquent `array` or `json` casts, and filter in PHP. 5.6 has no JSON column type.

rules.heading: Conventions that keep 5.6 working
rules.text: Leave `use_upsert_alias` unset, so `upsert()` uses `VALUES()`. The row alias that setting switches to needs MySQL 8.0.19.

rules.heading: Conventions that keep 5.6 working
rules.text: Rename a column with raw `DB::statement('ALTER TABLE ... CHANGE ...')`. Avoid `renameColumn` and `renameIndex`, which emit 5.7 syntax.

rules.heading: Conventions that keep 5.6 working
rules.text: Use `Schema::hasTable` only. Column introspection is not reliable on 5.6 (not yet confirmed on a 5.6 server).

rules.heading: Conventions that keep 5.6 working
rules.text: Skip `db:show` and `db:monitor`, and run one database-queue worker (or another driver if the platform offers one). 5.6 has no `SKIP LOCKED`, so a single worker avoids double-processing.

rules.heading: Conventions that keep 5.6 working
rules.text: Use `timestamp`, not `date`, for `useCurrent()`. A `date` column cannot take a current-timestamp default on 5.6.

rules.heading: Conventions that keep 5.6 working
rules.text: Run migrations in CI against a real 5.6 container. SQLite-only tests pass code that 5.6 rejects.

rules.heading: Dependencies
rules.text: No `dev-master`, `dev-*` or `*` constraints on runtime dependencies (ADR-0003).

rules.heading: Dependencies
rules.text: A lock file is required and must be committed (ADR-0003).

rules.heading: Dependencies
rules.text: `composer audit` must report no advisories at or above the policy's severity threshold (ADR-0003).

rules.heading: Dependencies
rules.text: `composer.json` `require.php` must not allow an EOL version as its lowest bound (ADR-0003).

rules.heading: Dependencies
rules.text: Every project is a framework-free core plus thin adapters. `composer.json` requires only `php` and PSR packages; Laravel, Inertia and Vue are `suggest` (ADR-0001).

rules.heading: Dependencies
rules.text: Adapters call the core and never re-implement it (ADR-0001).

rules.heading: Deploy gate
rules.text: The deploy-time rule set is small, offline and fast: the target image's status and its PHP version against `policy.json`, the framework and stack package versions in `composer.lock`, and known advisories from a cached database (ADR-0006).

rules.heading: Deploy gate
rules.text: EOL fails: a deploy that regresses a rule, a new app that fails any rule, or an expired override is blocked (ADR-0006).

rules.heading: Deploy gate
rules.text: It ratchets: a deploy that doesn't make things worse always passes (ADR-0006).

rules.heading: Deploy gate
rules.text: Each rule moves through stages, `report`, `warn`, `block`, with dates in `policy.json` (ADR-0006).

rules.heading: On Citadel
rules.text: Citadel runs the gate in its release hook: `proctor gate` in `runGitPull()`, against the fetched commit, before it is checked out (ADR-0006).

rules.heading: On Citadel
rules.text: The gate is pending the Citadel team (D-005). Until it is adopted, enforcement is CI on the test GitLab instance (ADR-0006).

rules.heading: Elsewhere
rules.text: The same gate runs as a CI job through PREFLIGHT's `proctor` component, wherever the pipeline runs (first-repos).

rules.heading: Elsewhere
rules.text: SQUIRE's `docker` target will run the gate before it ships an image, and so will its later `openshift` and `coolify` targets (ADR-0010).

rules.heading: Every OS
rules.text: Every developer tool works on Windows, macOS and Linux (ADR-0009).

rules.heading: Every OS
rules.text: A developer script ships as a `.ps1` and `.sh` pair that do the same thing, or as one PHP command, which works the same everywhere (ADR-0009).

rules.heading: Every OS
rules.text: Windows gets PowerShell (`.ps1`), which never needs bash or WSL. Linux and macOS get bash (`.sh`), written for macOS's stock bash 3.2 and its BSD tools (ADR-0009).

rules.heading: Every OS
rules.text: Every repo carries a `.gitattributes` with `* text=auto eol=lf`, and `.ps1`, `.bat` and `.cmd` set to CRLF. Anything that runs on a Linux host must be LF: on Citadel, and on OpenShift, Coolify or raw Docker elsewhere (ADR-0009).

rules.heading: Every OS
rules.text: Paths are built with the language's path functions, and subprocesses start with argument arrays, never shell strings (ADR-0009).

rules.heading: Overrides
rules.text: Overrides are named, dated and visible (ADR-0003).

rules.heading: Overrides
rules.text: An app keeps a `policy-overrides.json` with an expiry date and a reason (ADR-0003).

rules.heading: Overrides
rules.text: Check prints every override on every run, and Fleet lists them (ADR-0003).

rules.heading: Overrides
rules.text: An expired override is a failure (first-repos).

rules.heading: Overrides
rules.text: On the Citadel side, overrides are held by Citadel admins, per app and per rule, with an expiry, a reason and an approver. There is no permanent override (ADR-0006).

rules.heading: Runtime and headers
rules.text: The runtime (Baseline) is enforcement point (a): it warns, and refuses only for unsafe config (ADR-0002).

rules.heading: Runtime and headers
rules.text: The HELMET header work is to be decided.

rules.heading: Versions
rules.text: The dates live in `policy/policy.json`. Every tool derives a version's state from the date, through the CREED reader. No other code decides state (ADR-0003).

rules.heading: Versions
rules.text: The PHP floor is `^8.2`, the oldest non-EOL version today (ADR-0003). It moves to `^8.3` on 2027-01-01.

rules.heading: Versions
rules.text: Stack packages raise their own `php` floor in a new major when a PHP version reaches EOL, so security fixes require the upgrade (ADR-0003).

rules.heading: Versions
rules.text: `policy.json` is a contract, versioned like WayneUI's `/v2/`. Older Check versions must still read newer policy files (ADR-0003).

rules.heading: rules
rules.text: policy.json sets rules.audit_severity_threshold to "high".

rules.heading: rules

rules.heading: rules
rules.text: policy.json sets rules.eol_grace_days to 90.
